notes.source: src/app/lib/ipc-sync.js:109-140 lists rmrf, cp and mv among the fsFunctions the renderer may call, so a path the renderer passes over Electron IPC (a file name listed by the remote SSH/SFTP server) reaches them
notes.sink: src/app/lib/fs.js:114-118 rmrf builds `rm -rf "${localFolderPath}"` and calls run(cmd); :125-129 mv builds `mv '${from}' '${to}'`; :136-140 cp builds `cp -r "${from}" "${to}"`
notes.between: run() at fs.js:36-45 hands the string to node-bash's Bash.invokeCommand, and runWinCmd at :51-53 wraps it in a powershell command through execAsync(promisify(exec)); the POSIX path's shell call is an npm package's method, not child_process.exec or execa

notes.source: server/src/built-in-command/commands/download-command/download-command.ts:101-103 assetValue = context.args.slice(1).join(' ').trim(), the URL typed after '/download model'
notes.sink: server/src/built-in-command/commands/download-command/download-command.ts:170-177 fileName = getModelFileNameFromURL(assetValue); destinationPath = path.join(LLM_DIR_PATH, fileName); await FileHelper.downloadFile(assetValue, destinationPath, ...)
notes.between: getModelFileNameFromURL (:21-30) takes path.basename(parsedURL.pathname) and decodes it afterwards, so %2e%2e%2f survives the basename and becomes ../ only on the next line; path.basename() is exactly the name a scanner takes for a path sanitizer, and the write is a project helper (FileHelper.downloadFile) rather than fs.writeFile
notes.fix: decodes only the last raw path segment, rejects '.', '..' and both separators, then refuses a destination that resolves outside LLM_DIR_PATH
